Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the applicant works in a team. It's also a good way to see how the applicant handles conflict. Look for an answer that shows the applicant is willing to work with others and can handle difficult situations.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work with a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I was working on a project with a team of people from different departments. We were all working toward the same goal, but we had different ideas about how to get there. I was able to bring everyone together by getting them to focus on the end goal and not on their differences. I also made sure everyone was heard and understood. In the end, we were able to come up with a plan that worked for everyone.

Consultant.question: 97. What are Google's values?
Consultant.overview: Google is a technology company that is known for its unique corporate culture. This question tests the candidate's knowledge of the company and ability to explain how it aligns with Google's values.
expectations: Ability to articulate how the company's values align with the candidate's own
Knowledge of Google's history and mission
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Google is a technology company that has grown to be one of the most valuable companies in the world. It has a unique corporate culture that is based on innovation, collaboration and transparency. Employees are encouraged to think outside the box and take risks. Google has a flat organizational structure that promotes teamwork and collaboration. The company also strives to be environmentally friendly.

Consultant.question: 98. What would you do if you were unprepared for a client meeting?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant would handle a difficult situation. It's important to see how the applicant reacts to stress and pressure.
expectations: Applicant's ability to remain calm under pressure
Ability to think quickly on the spot
Ability to prioritize and make decisions
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first assess the situation and determine if I was unprepared because of a lack of research or if I had simply forgotten some key information. If it was the former, I would go back and do more research. If it was the latter, I would try to remember what I could. Then, I would ask the client for an extension on the meeting. If that wasn't possible, I would try my best to present my findings in a clear and concise way.

Consultant.question: 99. How would you design a Data warehouse?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of databases and data warehousing. It also shows how well the applicant can think on his or her feet. The answer should include a brief description of the process and the steps involved in designing a data warehouse.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think on his or her feet
Ability to work with large amounts of data
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Data warehouses are used to store large amounts of data. They are designed to make it easier for companies to access and analyze information. I would start by identifying the company's needs and goals. I would then create a list of all the data that would be needed for analysis. I would also identify any gaps in the data and determine how to fill those gaps. Finally, I would create a plan for how the data warehouse will be maintained and updated in the future.

Consultant.question: 100. What is your experience with Agile?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the industry and ability to explain their experience. It also gives you a chance to see how well they can communicate and how well they understand the concept of Agile.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've worked with Agile for several years. I've been involved in several projects that used Agile methodologies, including Scrum and Kanban. I've also led teams that used Agile. I think Agile is a great way to manage projects because it allows teams to adjust quickly to changing priorities and requirements. It also helps teams stay focused on the most important tasks at hand.

Consultant.question: 101. How do you handle difficult clients?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your ability to work with people and your communication skills. It also reveals how you handle conflict and whether you can work well with others.
expectations: Ability to work with difficult clients
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I think it's important to remember that everyone has a different perspective on a situation. I try to understand the client's point of view and look for common ground. If I can't find common ground, I try to understand why the client feels the way he or she does. I also try to be respectful of the client's time and schedule.

Consultant.question: 102. What is the reason for your low grades this semester?
Consultant.overview: This is a behavioral question that tests the applicant's honesty and integrity. The interviewer wants to see how the applicant will respond to a difficult question. The answer should be honest and show the applicant's willingness to take responsibility for mistakes.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I was working as a consultant for a company that was struggling with a few key issues. I was so focused on helping the company that I didn't give my studies the attention they needed. I realize now that I need to focus on my studies and make sure I'm prepared for the next semester.

Consultant.question: 103. How do you define success in your life?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant thinks about success. The answer should show a desire to achieve and a willingness to work hard. It should also show that the applicant has a plan for achieving success.
expectations: Ability to set goals and achieve them
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Success is defined by me as achieving my goals. I have a number of goals that I want to achieve in the next few years, including starting my own consultancy firm. I am working hard to achieve these goals, and I am confident I will succeed.

Consultant.question: 104. Why do you want to change your job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the applicant is looking for a new job because he or she is unhappy with the current one. It also reveals whether the applicant is motivated by money or career advancement.
expectations: Applicant's reasons for wanting to change jobs
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm looking for a new job because I want to expand my skill set and gain more experience. I'm interested in working with a company that has a strong reputation in the industry. I'm also eager to work with a company that can offer me opportunities for growth and advancement.

Consultant.question: 105. Tell me about your experience in leading a project and the outcome.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate has handled leadership roles in the past and what kind of results they've achieved. Applicants should focus on a project they've led and how they managed it.
expectations: Applicant's ability to lead a project from start to finish
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I led a project for a large company that was looking to expand its operations into Asia. I was responsible for developing a plan for the company's expansion, which included identifying key markets and potential partners. I worked with the company's leaders to develop a strategy that would allow it to enter new markets and expand its business. The project was successful and the company is now in the process of expanding into Asia.

Consultant.question: 106. What are your future plans?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the applicant has a clear idea of where he or she wants to go in the future. It also shows whether the applicant has a long-term plan or is just looking for a job.
expectations: Ability to plan for the future
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm interested in working with a company that offers me the opportunity to develop my skills and advance my career. I'm looking for a company that will help me grow into a leadership role and provide me with opportunities to take on more responsibility. I want to work with a company that will help me achieve my career goals.

Consultant.question: 107. Why are you leaving your current job?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to be honest and professional. The interviewer wants to know if the candidate is leaving for a better opportunity or because of a conflict. The answer should be positive and show the applicant is looking forward to the next step in his or her career.
expectations: Ability to explain why he or she is leaving without sounding negative
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm leaving my current job because I'm ready for a new challenge. I've learned a lot at my current company, and I'm ready to put that knowledge to work in a new environment. I'm excited about the opportunity with your company and look forward to contributing my skills and experience.

Consultant.question: 108. Tell me about a person that you had difficulty working with.
Consultant.overview: This question tests the candidate's ability to work with others and their interpersonal skills. The answer also shows the candidate's ability to handle conflict and resolve issues.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once worked with a team member who was very talented but had a difficult personality. He was very critical of others' work and often made them feel bad. I was able to work with him because I was able to build a trusting relationship with him. I was honest about my feelings and he was able to understand how his behavior affected others. We were able to work together and he became more open-minded and respectful of others' opinions.

Consultant.question: 109. Describe a project in Change Management you have led.
Consultant.overview: Change management is a broad term that encompasses many different types of projects. This question is designed to see how well applicants can tailor their responses to the specific type of project they're being asked about. The answer should show the applicant's knowledge of the industry and ability to work in a team.
expectations: Applicant's ability to tailor answers to specific project types
Ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I led a project in change management at a large company that was in the process of merging with another company. The company was undergoing a lot of changes, including new leadership, which meant employees were feeling anxious and unsure about the future. I worked with the leaders to develop a strategy for communicating with employees and helping them understand how the merger would affect them. I also worked with employees directly, helping them understand what to expect and how they could prepare for the changes ahead.

Consultant.question: 110. Tell me about a time when you had to convince your manager that your view was the correct one.
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to communicate effectively and work well with others. It also reveals how the applicant approaches conflict and shows how they handle stress.
expectations: Ability to work well with others
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I had a situation where I was working with a group of people on a project. I was in charge of the project, but I had to work with a team of people who were not familiar with my work style. I had to convince them that my way of doing things was the best way. I did this by being open and honest about my process and showing them how it would help the team meet its goals.

Consultant.question: 111. What was the last conflict you had with a client?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate deals with conflict. It also shows how well the applicant can communicate and work with others.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I recently had a conflict with a client over the scope of a project. The client wanted me to complete the project in less time than I had estimated. I explained that I could not complete the project in the time frame they wanted without sacrificing quality. The client was not happy with my response, but I stood my ground. In the end, we compromised on a schedule that was acceptable to both of us.

Consultant.question: 112. How would you approach a CEO?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your ability to think on your feet and communicate effectively. The answer should show that you have a solid understanding of the CEO's role in the company and how you would approach him or her.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think on their feet
Knowledge of the CEO's role in the company
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first do some research on the company and its CEO. I would then schedule a meeting with the CEO and make sure I was prepared with a few key talking points. I would also want to know what the CEO's goals are for the company and how my work could help him or her achieve those goals.

Consultant.question: 113. What experience do you have in the pharmaceutical industry?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your knowledge of the industry and your ability to think on your feet. It also shows how well you can explain your experience and how you can add value to a company.
expectations: Applicant's knowledge of the pharmaceutical industry
Ability to explain how their experience can be applied to a new company
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've worked with pharmaceutical companies for more than 10 years. I've worked with large firms and small startups. I've helped companies develop strategies for growth and improve their bottom line. I've also helped companies develop new products and bring them to market. I'm very familiar with the industry and the challenges it faces.

Consultant.question: 114. What kind of data would you prefer to work with?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the industry and how they prefer to work with data. The answer should show an understanding of the different types of data and how they can be used.
expectations: Applicant's preference for working with certain types of data
Ability to understand and analyze data
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I prefer to work with qualitative data. I think it's more useful in the long run because it helps me understand the underlying reasons for a problem or opportunity. Quantitative data is great for measuring performance, but it doesn't always give me a complete picture of what's going on.

Consultant.question: 115. What is the notice period of your current job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant handles a potentially uncomfortable situation. It's important to hire people who are honest and direct.
expectations: Applicant's ability to be honest and direct
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have a two-week notice period with my current employer.

Consultant.question: 116. Tell me about a time you resolved a conflict in a group setting.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well you can handle conflict. It's important for consultants to be able to work with others and resolve issues. This question is also a good way to see how well you can communicate and work with others.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I recently worked on a project with a team of people from different departments. We had to come together to solve a problem that was affecting the entire company. We were all very passionate about our ideas, but we had to find a solution that everyone could agree on. I was able to help the team reach a compromise by listening to everyone's opinions and coming up with a solution that everyone felt good about.

Consultant.question: 117. How will you write a query for the given situation?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to write a query letter. The query is the first document a consultant sends to a potential client. It should be short and to the point, highlighting the consultant's experience and expertise.
expectations: Applicant's ability to write a concise and persuasive query letter
Ability to tailor the query to the client's needs
Ability to research the client and demonstrate understanding of their business
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would begin by introducing myself and my firm. I would then explain why I am writing and what I have to offer. I would then describe my experience and expertise in the area of consulting that is relevant to the client's needs. I would conclude by asking for an opportunity to speak with the client about my qualifications.

Consultant.question: 118. Why are you looking for a new job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test the applicant's honesty and integrity. Candidates should be prepared to explain why they are looking for a new job and how it will benefit the company.
expectations: Ability to explain why they are looking for a new job
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm looking for a new job because I want to work for a company that has the same values as I do. I believe in hard work and doing what's best for the customer. I also want to work for a company that has a strong commitment to its employees. I've been working as a consultant for several years and have learned a lot about business and how companies operate. I'm ready to take my knowledge and apply it in a new environment.

Consultant.question: 119. Why do you want to be a consultant?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the applicant has done research on the industry and understands what it takes to succeed. The answer should show that the applicant is passionate about the field and has a clear idea of what it takes to succeed.
expectations: Motivation for entering the consulting field
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've always been fascinated by how businesses work and how they can be improved. I've worked with a number of companies over the years, and I've seen firsthand how consultants can help them improve performance. I want to be a consultant because I enjoy working with businesses and helping them grow.

Consultant.question: 120. What is your dream job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant thinks about their career. It's a good way to see whether they are motivated by money or by the work itself.
expectations: Applicant's willingness to take on new challenges and learn new skills
Consultant.sampleAnswer: My dream job would be to work as a consultant for a company that is passionate about its products and services. I want to work with a company that is committed to its customers and has a strong vision for the future. I want to be able to work with a team that is willing to push the boundaries of what's possible and help the company grow.

Consultant.question: 121. Tell me about a time when you had to make an unpopular decision.
Consultant.overview: This question tests how well applicants can handle conflict and difficult situations. It also gives you insight into the applicant's leadership skills and ability to make tough calls.
expectations: Applicant's ability to make unpopular decisions
Ability to lead others through a difficult situation
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I had to make an unpopular decision when I was working with a client who was struggling with a new product launch. The client was having trouble getting the product into stores, and I had to tell the client that we needed to change the product's packaging. The client didn't want to hear it, but I knew it was the right decision. We ended up changing the packaging, and the product became a huge success.

Consultant.question: 122. What do you know about change management?
Consultant.overview: Change management is a critical part of any consulting project. Companies hire consultants to bring about change, and the consultant must be able to manage that change. This question tests the applicant's knowledge of change management and ability to explain how he or she would handle it.
expectations: Applicant's understanding of the importance of change management
Ability to explain how he or she would handle change management
Ability to explain how he or she would handle resistance to change
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Change management is an important part of any consulting project. It's the process of helping employees adjust to new processes, procedures and systems. Change management is often necessary when a company is implementing new technology or changing its business model. I think the most important part of change management is communication. Consultants must be able to clearly communicate the changes that are coming and why they're necessary. They must also be able to listen to employees' concerns and address them in a way that makes them feel heard.

Consultant.question: 123. What skills do you have to pursue as a consultant?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your knowledge of the skills needed to succeed as a consultant. It also reveals whether you have researched the profession and are familiar with the skills that are most important.
expectations: Applicant's understanding of the skills needed to be a consultant
Ability to explain how they will acquire those skills
Knowledge of the industry and its trends
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have a strong background in business and finance, which will help me understand the company's goals and how I can help achieve them. I also have experience in sales, which will help me sell my services to clients. I am a quick learner and have excellent communication skills. I am also a self-starter who can work independently and manage my time effectively.

Consultant.question: 124. What challenges do you foresee?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to think critically and anticipate problems. It also shows whether the candidate has done any research on your company.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I see a few challenges ahead. First, I think the company is going to need to make some changes in its leadership structure. I've noticed that the company is very siloed and that communication is lacking. I think the company will need to make some changes in order to be more efficient.

Consultant.question: 125. How would you handle a situation where client wants you implement a particular solution but your team does not think it will be effective and presents another solution?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to handle conflict and build consensus. It also reveals how the candidate thinks about client satisfaction. Look for an answer that shows the applicant is willing to listen to others and consider their ideas.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first make sure my team and I understand the client's goals and objectives. Then, I would explain our concerns and offer an alternative solution. I would also suggest a trial period so we can test the effectiveness of the solution. If the client is not satisfied with our solution, we will work together to find a better one.

Consultant.question: 126. How did you help yourself to learn quickly during your internship?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant learns and grows. The interviewer wants to know how the applicant will take on new challenges and responsibilities.
expectations: Ability to adapt to new situations
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I always made sure I was prepared for meetings and presentations. I read up on the company and the industry, and I learned about the company's goals and challenges. I also made sure to ask questions during meetings and take notes so I could review them later.

Consultant.question: 127. What was a time you worked in a group with conflict?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to work with others and resolve issues. It also gives you insight into the candidate's personality and how he or she deals with conflict.
expectations: Ability to be a team player
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very outgoing person and I enjoy working with others. I've never had a problem working in a group, but there have been times when I've had to deal with conflict. In one situation, I was working on a team that was having trouble coming to a consensus on a project. I stepped in and helped the team reach an agreement by encouraging everyone to express their opinions. I also helped the team come up with solutions that would work for everyone.

Consultant.question: 128. Tell me about a time when you had to deliver something in a timeline that was not possible?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to think on their feet and come up with a solution. It also shows how they handle pressure and whether they can deliver under pressure.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think quickly and solve problems
Ability to prioritize and manage time
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once had to deliver a project that was due in two weeks. The client was very clear that the project needed to be done in two weeks, but I knew it would take me longer than that. I met with the client and explained that I could deliver the project in two weeks, but it would be of lower quality than if I had more time. The client agreed to give me more time, and I delivered the project on time and within budget.

Consultant.question: 129. How would you deal with being in a hotel every night for the next few months?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant will react to a situation that may be uncomfortable. It's important for consultants to be able to work independently and not be distracted by factors outside their control.
expectations: Ability to adapt to new situations
Ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very independent person, so I'm not worried about being in a hotel for a few months. I'm sure it will be a little strange at first, but I'm sure I'll get used to it. I know that the company wants me to be as productive as possible, so I'll make sure to get a good night's sleep and work hard during the day.

Consultant.question: 130. Give me examples of complex situations that you have managed.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates handle pressure and difficult situations. It also tests their ability to think on their feet and come up with solutions. Applicants should focus on situations that show their problem-solving skills, leadership and ability to work with other people.
expectations: Ability to think critically and creatively
Ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've managed several complex situations in my career. One of my first projects was for a large company that wanted to expand into a new market. I was tasked with helping the company develop a plan for entering the new market and making recommendations for the best approach. I had to work with several departments within the company, as well as outside consultants, to develop a strategy that would be successful. The project took several months, but we were able to come up with a plan that was approved by the board of directors.

Consultant.question: 131. How will you design a fault tolerant application or service?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test your knowledge of computer science and software development. It's also a good way to see how you think through problems and how well you can communicate your ideas.
expectations: Applicant's ability to design a fault tolerant application or service
Knowledge of computer science and software development
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first identify the most common faults that could occur in the application or service. Then I would design the system to handle those faults. For example, if the system is supposed to send an email, I would make sure it can handle a server crash or network failure. I would also make sure the system can handle a large number of users at once.

Consultant.question: 132. How would you approach a project of this sort?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to think critically and address specific issues. The answer should show a clear understanding of the project and the steps the applicant would take to complete it.
expectations: Ability to follow a project from start to finish
Ability to research and understand the project
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first do some research on the company and its goals. I would then talk with the company's leadership to understand their vision for the project. I would also want to speak with employees who will be involved in the project so I can get a better idea of what they need from me. After that, I would create a plan for completing the project and set deadlines for each step. I would also make sure to keep everyone involved in the loop as I progress through the project.

Consultant.question: 133. What is the software development life cycle?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of software development and the SDLC. The SDLC is a process that software developers use to create, test and deploy software. It's important for consultants to understand this process and how it can be applied to different types of projects.
expectations: Ability to apply the SDLC to different types of projects
Ability to explain the SDLC in a way that is easy to understand
Consultant.sampleAnswer: The software development life cycle is a process that software developers use to create, test and deploy software. It's important for consultants to understand this process and how it can be applied to different types of projects. The SDLC consists of five steps: analysis, design, implementation, testing and deployment. Each step has its own purpose and is critical to the success of the project.

Consultant.question: 134. How do you work in a team?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the candidate can work with others. It also reveals whether the applicant has a collaborative or independent style. Look for an answer that shows the applicant can work well with others and is able to communicate effectively.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm a big believer in teamwork. I think it's important for consultants to be able to work with others and share ideas. I've found that when consultants work together, they can come up with better solutions and ideas than they could alone. That's why I'm always open to working with others and sharing my ideas.

Consultant.question: 135. What do you expect from the job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the candidate understands the role and the company. The answer should show the applicant's interest in the position and understanding of what will be expected of them.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm looking for a position that will allow me to use my skills and experience to help a company achieve its goals. I'm interested in a position that will allow me to work with a variety of clients and projects. I'm also looking for a company that values teamwork and collaboration.

Consultant.question: 136. What are the likely macro economic developments and how should Cognizant position itself in global markets?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the industry and ability to think critically about the future. The answer should show the candidate's ability to analyze trends and make predictions.
expectations: Applicant's ability to analyze macroeconomic trends
Ability to think critically about the future
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I believe the global economy will continue to grow at a steady pace. I think the biggest challenge for Cognizant will be keeping up with demand for its services. I think Cognizant should focus on expanding its services in emerging markets, especially in Asia. I think Cognizant should also invest in research and development to ensure it stays ahead of the curve.

Consultant.question: 137. What courses did you take in college that will help you with this position?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the skills needed for the job. It also shows how well the applicant researched the company and position.
expectations: Applicant's knowledge of the skills needed for the job
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I took a number of courses in college that will help me with this position. I took a class on business strategy that taught me how to identify and solve problems. I also took a class on marketing that taught me how to develop a brand and promote it effectively. I think these skills will help me do my job well.

Consultant.question: 138. What are your strengths and weaknesses?
Consultant.overview: This is a classic interview question, but it's still one of the most important. The answer should be honest and show the candidate's ability to self-evaluate. Look for an answer that shows the applicant is aware of his or her weaknesses and is working to improve them.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm very organized and detail-oriented. I'm also very good at building relationships with clients and colleagues. My weakness is that I can be too focused on the details. I need to remember that sometimes it's more important to look at the big picture.

Consultant.question: 139. How did you go about getting help on a project?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate approaches problems and how he or she works with others. The answer should show that the candidate is proactive and willing to seek help when needed.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work with others
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I always try to solve problems on my own first. If I can't solve the problem, I reach out to my manager or a colleague for help. I like to work independently, but I also know that sometimes it's better to ask for help.

Consultant.question: 140. Where do you see yourself fitting in?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the candidate understands the role of a consultant. Applicants should be able to explain how they will contribute to the company and what they can do to help it achieve its goals.
expectations: Applicant's understanding of the role of a consultant
Ability to explain how they will contribute to the company
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I see myself as a valuable asset to your company. I am a skilled problem-solver who will work with your team to identify issues and find solutions. I will also work with you to develop a plan that will help you achieve your goals.

Consultant.question: 141. Why did you choose NCS?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test your knowledge of the company and your interest in working for it. It's also a chance for you to show your enthusiasm and interest in the position.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I chose NCS because I've heard great things about the company and its work environment. I've also heard that you're a leader in the industry and that you're committed to helping your clients succeed. I think this is a great opportunity for me to learn more about the industry and make a difference in my career.

Consultant.question: 142. Q: What types of tools or technologies have you used in the past that is related to security?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test the candidate's knowledge of security and their ability to think on their feet. The interviewer wants to see whether the applicant can think of examples quickly and respond appropriately.
expectations: Ability to think on their feet
Knowledge of security tools and technologies
Knowledge of the company's security needs
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've used a variety of security tools in the past. I've worked with firewalls, intrusion detection systems and antivirus software. I've also used encryption software and remote access tools. I know that your company uses a firewall, but you may want to consider upgrading to a more advanced system.

Consultant.question: 143. What kind of experience do you have?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to gauge the applicant's experience in the consulting industry. Look for an answer that shows the applicant has experience working with companies in your industry and has a good understanding of your company's needs.
expectations: Ability to work with your company's specific needs
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have worked with several companies in the manufacturing industry, including yours. I understand how manufacturing companies operate and what they need to succeed. I've worked with a variety of different companies, from small startups to large corporations. I've also worked on projects that have helped companies grow and expand into new markets.

Consultant.question: 144. What is your business requirements document?
Consultant.overview: A business requirements document (BRD) is a document that describes the business problem or opportunity that a consulting firm is being hired to solve. It should be written in a way that is clear and easy to understand. This question tests the applicant's ability to write clearly and concisely.
expectations: Applicant's ability to write clearly and concisely
Ability to organize thoughts and ideas
Consultant.sampleAnswer: A business requirements document (BRD) is a document that describes the business problem or opportunity that a consulting firm is being hired to solve. It should be written in a way that is clear and easy to understand. This question tests the applicant's ability to write clearly and concisely.

Consultant.question: 145. What are you most proud of in your life?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate thinks about their own accomplishments and how they reflect on their life. It's also a way to learn more about the candidate's personality and values.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think about their accomplishments
Ability to reflect on their life and career
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm most proud of my decision to start my own business. I took a risk and it paid off. I also love the fact that I can work from home and be with my family.

Consultant.question: 146. Tell me about a situation when you had to deal with a difficult requirement from your client?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates handle conflict. It also gives you insight into their communication skills and ability to work with clients.
expectations: Applicant's ability to communicate and negotiate with clients
Ability to deal with difficult clients
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've had to deal with a difficult requirement from my client when I was working on a project for a large company. The client wanted me to design a new system that would be used by thousands of employees. The problem was that the company didn't have the budget to hire a large team of developers. I had to work with the client to come up with a solution that would provide the same functionality as a larger system but at a lower cost.

Consultant.question: 147. What macro economic data do you use?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the industry and how macroeconomic factors affect the business. It also tests whether the applicant has done research on your company and industry.
expectations: Applicant's knowledge of macroeconomic data and how it affects the business
Ability to do research and prepare for interviews
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Macroeconomic data is useful for predicting consumer behavior and company performance. I use this information to help clients understand how their business will be affected by changes in the economy. For example, I might look at unemployment rates or inflation numbers to predict how consumers will react to certain products or services. I also use macroeconomic data to help clients make decisions about their business strategy. For example, if I see that interest rates are going up, I might suggest that my client consider refinancing its debt.

Consultant.question: 148. How do you deal with failure?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate handles adversity. It's important to see how the applicant responds to failure and how they learn from it.
expectations: Applicant's ability to take responsibility for failure
Ability to bounce back from failure
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I don't think of failure as a negative thing. I think of it as a learning experience. I've learned that sometimes you have to fail in order to succeed. The key is to learn from your mistakes and not repeat them.

Consultant.question: 149. What do you know about the company?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's research skills and interest in your company. Applicants should demonstrate they have done their homework and can speak intelligently about your business.
expectations: Applicant's level of interest in your company
Knowledge of your company's products, services and industry
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I know you're a publicly traded company with a market cap of $10 billion. You have a diverse portfolio of products and services, including software, hardware, consulting and training. Your revenue has grown by 10% over the past year. I've read about your recent acquisitions and partnerships in the news. I also know you're committed to improving customer service and increasing sales.

Consultant.question: 150. Which conferences do you attend?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see if the applicant is keeping up with the latest trends in the industry. It also shows whether the candidate is networking and building relationships with peers.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I attend a number of conferences each year. I find that these events are great for networking and gaining insight into new trends and technologies. I also like to attend conferences that offer continuing education credits, which help me maintain my certifications.

Consultant.question: 151. What are the three attributes of a leader you did not like in previous jobs, and how did you go about them?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant handles difficult situations. It's also a chance to see how the applicant thinks about leadership. Look for an answer that shows the candidate has a strong sense of self and can work with others.
expectations: Ability to work with difficult people
Ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've worked with leaders who were too controlling, too critical and too negative. I've learned that it's important to be open to new ideas and suggestions, but it's also important to be able to make decisions and take charge when necessary. I've learned that it's important to be honest and direct with people, but also kind and understanding. I've learned that it's important to be a good listener, but also able to speak up when necessary.

Consultant.question: 152. What R package have you used to visualize results?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of data visualization. It also shows whether the candidate has experience with R and is familiar with the most popular packages.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've used the ggplot2 package to visualize results. It's a powerful package that allows users to create a variety of charts and graphs. I've also used the lattice package to create trellis charts.

Consultant.question: 153. What happens when you load the data on the same cell with 2 different data values.
Consultant.overview: This question tests the candidate's knowledge of Excel. It also tests their ability to think on their feet and come up with a solution quickly.
expectations: Ability to think on their feet
Consultant.sampleAnswer: When you try to enter data on a cell that already has data, Excel will display a warning message. If you enter the data anyway, the cell will display the #VALUE! error. You can either delete the data in the cell or change it to a different value.

Consultant.question: 154. Tell me about a time when you had to negotiate with someone.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well you can negotiate with others. It's important for consultants to be able to negotiate with clients and vendors, as well as within their own company. Look for an answer that shows the applicant is skilled at negotiating and has experience doing so.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I had to negotiate with a vendor who was asking for a higher price than I was willing to pay. I knew that if I paid the higher price, I would be losing money on the project. I approached the vendor and explained why I couldn't pay more. We talked about the project and what it entailed. We were able to reach a compromise that was beneficial for both of us.

Consultant.question: 155. How would you increase ice-cream sales in the street during winter?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to think creatively and solve problems. It also shows how well the candidate can work in a team.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think creatively and solve problems
Ability to work well in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first look at the data and analyze the problem. I would then do some research to see if there is a way to increase sales during winter. I would look at other ice-cream brands and see what they are doing to increase sales. I would also talk to customers and ask them why they don't buy ice-cream during winter. I would then come up with a solution that will increase sales.

Consultant.question: 156. Why do you want to join our consulting team?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to find out whether the candidate is a good fit for your company. The applicant should show enthusiasm for your company's mission and values.
expectations: Ability to communicate and work well with others
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've been following your company for some time now and have been impressed with your growth and success. I'm excited about the opportunity to join your team and help you achieve even greater success. I'm a hard worker who is passionate about helping companies improve their performance. I'm also a great collaborator who can work well with others.

Consultant.question: 157. How will you launch a new product?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's understanding of the business and its goals. The answer should show the applicant's ability to think critically and address the company's needs.
expectations: Ability to think critically and address issues
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Launching a new product can be a difficult process. It is important to consider all aspects of the product, including its price, quality and features. I would first assess the market to see if there is a need for this product. If there is, I would then determine if it is priced appropriately. If it is not, I would recommend changes to the price or features. Once I am satisfied with the product, I would begin marketing it to potential customers.

Consultant.question: 158. Do you prefer to work alone or in a team?
Consultant.overview: Consultants are hired to work on projects that require a specific skill set or knowledge base. They should be able to work independently, but also be able to collaborate with others. This question tests the applicant's ability to work in a team environment and communicate effectively with others.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work in a team environment
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I prefer to work in a team environment. I think it's important for consultants to be able to work independently, but I also believe it's important for them to be able to collaborate with others. I think working in a team environment helps me learn from others and grow my skills. It also helps me build relationships with people in the organization.

Consultant.question: 159. What do you think about doing an MBA?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the applicant has a plan for their career and is thinking about their future. It also shows whether the applicant has done research on your company and the industry.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I think an MBA would be a great next step for me. I've always been interested in business and I think it would help me gain a better understanding of the industry. I've also heard that an MBA can help you land a job at a top consulting firm.

Consultant.question: 160. Tell me about a challenge you faced and how did you overcome it?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test your ability to overcome challenges and learn from mistakes. It also gives you insight into the applicant's character and work ethic.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I was working on a project for a large company and was tasked with creating a new product. I had a lot of experience in the field, but I had never worked on this type of project before. I was excited to take on the challenge, but I quickly realized that I was in over my head. I didn't have the right resources or support to get the job done. I had to step back and reassess my approach. I ended up reaching out to a colleague who had experience with this type of project and asked him for help. He was able to guide me through the process and help me complete the project successfully.

Consultant.question: 161. Will you be willing to travel?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the candidate is willing to travel for work. It also reveals whether the applicant has done research on the company and its industry.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm willing to travel within reason. I know that travel can be a big part of this job, but I want to make sure that it doesn't take away from my family time. I've done a lot of research on your company and your industry, and I know that you have a lot of clients in other states. If you need me to travel, I'm happy to do it.

Consultant.question: 162. What do you know about our company?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your knowledge of the company and its industry. It also shows how much research you have done on the business. Applicants should be able to show they have done their homework and are prepared for the interview.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've been following your company for a while now and have been impressed with its growth and success. I've read about your products and services, and I'm familiar with your competitors. I think you're doing a great job in the industry, and I'm excited to learn more about how you operate.

Consultant.question: 163. What was the most challenging experience you have had?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates handle adversity. They should discuss a time when they had to overcome a difficult situation and explain what they learned from the experience.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once worked with a client who was very demanding and hard to please. It was challenging because I had to meet his high expectations while still maintaining my own standards. I learned that it's important to be flexible and adaptable when working with different clients.

Consultant.question: 164. What would you do if your manager took credit for your idea?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to work with others. It also reveals the applicant's level of confidence and willingness to speak up.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would approach my manager and talk about the issue. I would explain that I had come up with the idea and ask for credit. If he or she refused, I would ask for a meeting with our boss. I would explain the situation and ask for help in resolving it.

Consultant.question: 165. How do you value an infrastructure asset?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the consulting industry and ability to apply it to a real-world scenario. The answer should show the applicant's understanding of the process and ability to work with clients to solve problems.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: The first step in valuing an infrastructure asset is to determine its condition. This can be done by performing a physical inspection or by reviewing documentation. Next, the asset's remaining useful life must be determined. This is done by estimating how much time is left before the asset needs to be replaced or repaired. The value of the asset is then calculated by subtracting the asset's remaining useful life from its current value.

Consultant.question: 166. Tell me about a time when you faced difficulties.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the applicant handles challenges. It's important to see how the applicant responds to failure and what he or she learned from the experience.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once had a client who was very difficult to work with. He was demanding and critical, and he didn't seem to appreciate my work. I was frustrated and disappointed, but I realized that I needed to keep my cool and focus on the end goal. I had to remember that he was paying me for my expertise and that I needed to do my best work. In the end, I delivered a great product and he was happy.

Consultant.question: 167. What experience do you have in client-facing?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the candidate has experience interacting with clients. It is important for consultants to be able to communicate effectively and build trust with clients.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have worked with clients in a variety of industries, including retail, manufacturing and healthcare. I have also worked with clients in a variety of roles, from CEO to CFO. I am comfortable working with all levels of an organization and have a proven track record of building strong relationships.

Consultant.question: 168. What was the biggest failure in your life?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant reacts to failure. The applicant should discuss what they learned from the experience and how they would handle similar situations in the future.
expectations: Applicant's ability to learn from mistakes
Ability to take responsibility for mistakes
Ability to learn from past experiences
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once worked on a project that was very important to my company. I was in charge of the project and had a lot of responsibility. Unfortunately, I didn't do my research well enough and made a few mistakes. The client was not happy with the work and I had to redo the project. It was a big failure for me because I let my company down. I learned a lot from this experience. First, I learned that it's important to do my research thoroughly before starting a project. Second, I learned that it's important to be honest with clients about any potential issues or problems.

Consultant.question: 169. Briefly tell me about your background.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well applicants can communicate their experience and skills. They should be able to clearly summarize their career, including any education, training and work experience.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I graduated from the University of Michigan with a degree in marketing. I spent the first few years of my career working for a large consumer goods company, where I gained experience in brand management and product development. I then moved into consulting, where I worked with a variety of clients in the consumer goods industry. I've been working as a consultant for the past five years, helping companies develop and execute marketing strategies.

Consultant.question: 170. Case 2 - Why should the firm not do a JV or have an SLA?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the industry and ability to think critically. The interviewer is looking for an answer that shows the applicant understands the potential pitfalls of a joint venture or service level agreement.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I think a joint venture is a great idea. It will help the company expand its reach into new markets and increase sales. However, I think the company should be careful to not give up too much control over its operations. The company should also be careful to not give away its intellectual property. A service level agreement is a good idea because it will help the company manage its new partner. However, it's important that the company not agree to anything that will compromise its ability to succeed in the market.

Consultant.question: 171. What do you know about IBM?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your knowledge of the company and your ability to research a potential employer. It also shows whether you're interested in the position and have done your homework.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I know that IBM is a global technology and consulting company that has been around for decades. I know that it has a large presence in the financial services industry. I also know that it has been working on big data projects for quite some time and is now looking to expand into other industries.

Consultant.question: 172. What are your motivations?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well you understand your own motivations. It also tests your ability to articulate your goals and ambitions.
expectations: Applicant's ability to articulate personal motivations
Ability to explain how their motivations align with the company's goals
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm motivated by the opportunity to work with a variety of companies and industries. I'm also driven by the chance to make a difference in the world. I want to help companies grow and improve their performance.

Consultant.question: 173. How do you deal with regulators?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your understanding of the regulatory environment and how you can work with it. The answer also shows how you can work with other parties to achieve a goal.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work with regulators
Ability to work with other parties
Ability to understand and navigate complex regulatory environments
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have experience working with regulators in a variety of industries. I think the best way to deal with regulators is to be honest and transparent. If you're open about your company's practices and willing to work with regulators, they are more likely to be open to your ideas.

Consultant.question: 174. What is your educational background?
Consultant.overview: This question is a good way to gauge the applicant's level of education and experience. It's also a good way to see if the applicant has done his or her research on your company.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Michigan. I also have an MBA from the University of Chicago. I've been working in the consulting industry for five years and have been self-employed for three.

Consultant.question: 175. Tell me about a time when you had to lead a group of people.
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to work with others and manage a team. The answer should show the candidate's ability to communicate and motivate others.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've led a team of four people for the past three years. We work on a variety of projects, including market research, competitive analysis and strategic planning. I've learned that leading a team is all about communication and motivation. I make sure everyone on my team understands the goals of the project and what they need to do to achieve them. I also make sure they know how their work fits into the bigger picture. I'm always available to answer questions and help out when needed.

Consultant.question: 176. What is the difference between an inner and outer join in SQL?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of database technology. The answer should include an explanation of the difference between the two types of joins and how they are used.
expectations: Ability to explain technical concepts in layman's terms
Consultant.sampleAnswer: An inner join is used to find records that match in both tables. It returns all records from both tables that have matching values in the join columns. An outer join is used to find records that match in either table. It returns all records from both tables that have matching values in the join columns. Outer joins are often used when you want to see all possible records, even if they don't have a match in the other table.

Consultant.question: 177. How will you determine the liability of a specific insurance company?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your knowledge of insurance and your ability to think critically. The applicant should show an understanding of the process for determining liability and explain how they would approach the task.
expectations: Ability to analyze and assess data
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would begin by gathering all the information I could about the incident. I would then speak with the insurance company to learn more about its policies and procedures. I would also speak with the client to learn more about what happened. I would then consider all the information and determine whether the insurance company was liable for the accident. If it was, I would work with the client to determine how much money they should receive in compensation.

Consultant.question: 178. Tell me about a time when you had to deal with conflict at work.
Consultant.overview: Conflict is inevitable in any workplace. This question tests the applicant's ability to handle conflict and work with others. It also shows the interviewer how the applicant handles stress and handles criticism.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once worked on a project with a team of people who were all very different from one another. We had a difficult time getting along at first, but we eventually learned to appreciate each other's strengths and weaknesses. We learned how to work together and support each other. I think the key was being open and honest with each other. We had to be able to talk about our differences and work through them.

Consultant.question: 179. If you were working on a project and one of your team members wasn't carrying their weight, how would you respond to this issue?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant handles conflict and teamwork. The interviewer wants to know how the applicant will handle a situation in which a colleague is not pulling his or her weight. The applicant should demonstrate an understanding of the importance of teamwork and be able to explain how he or she would address the issue.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first talk with the person and find out what was going on. If it was a temporary issue, I would give them some time to get back on track. If it was a more serious problem, I would talk with my manager about the issue and see if there was anything we could do to help. If it was a recurring problem, I would probably have a conversation with the person about whether they wanted to continue working on the project.

Consultant.question: 180. What is your experience working in a group?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well applicants work in a team environment. It's important for consultants to be able to work with others, especially when they're working on a project with a client.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work in a team
Ability to work on a project with a client
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've worked on many projects with teams of people. I enjoy working in groups because it allows me to learn from others and build relationships. I think it's important for consultants to be able to work with others because it allows them to bring in different perspectives and ideas. I've found that working in groups helps me develop my skills and gain new knowledge.

Consultant.question: 181. How would you migrate a hospital IT system located on two sites into one site?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to think on their feet and problem-solve. It also shows whether they have experience working in a healthcare setting. Applicants should describe a plan for how they would approach the project, including any challenges they might face and how they would overcome them.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think on their feet and problem-solve
Experience working in a healthcare setting
Ability to work with a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: This type of migration is very complex. I would first need to understand the hospital's goals and objectives for the project. I would then need to understand the current IT infrastructure and how it is being used. I would also need to understand the hospital's budget and any time constraints. I would then begin by evaluating the current system to determine if it is meeting the hospital's needs. I would also evaluate the current IT infrastructure and determine if it is scalable. If not, I would recommend upgrading or adding new hardware or software. Once I have evaluated the current system, I would begin planning for the migration. I would first create a detailed plan that outlines all of the steps involved in migrating the system from one site to another. I would also create a timeline for completing each step of the project. I would then present my plan to hospital leadership for approval. Once approved, I would begin working on the project, keeping in close contact with hospital leadership to ensure that my team and I are on track with our timeline.

Consultant.question: 182. Tell me about a time when you had to rely on your team?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test how well the candidate can work with others. It also shows how the candidate handles stressful situations. The applicant should discuss a time when he or she had to rely on others for support and explain how the team came together to overcome the challenge.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once worked on a project that required me to travel to a different country. I was working with a team in the US and one in Europe. We were all working on different aspects of the project, but we had to come together at the end to present our findings. I had to rely on my team members for support, and they were able to help me complete the project successfully.

Consultant.question: 183. What would you do if the time ran out, but you're not happy with the quality of your work?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your ability to prioritize and deliver quality work. It also shows how you handle pressure and stress.
expectations: Ability to deliver quality work under pressure
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would stop working immediately and talk with my supervisor. I would explain the situation and ask for more time. I would also ask for help from other team members if necessary. I would do everything in my power to deliver the best possible product within the time frame given.

Consultant.question: 184. What was the most difficult problem you have encountered and how did you solve it?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your ability to think on your feet and problem-solve. It also shows how you handle pressure and how you react to failure. Applicants should focus on a problem they encountered at work and explain how they solved it.
expectations: Ability to learn from mistakes and improve performance
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once had a client who was unhappy with the work I was doing. He said I wasn't meeting his expectations. I knew I could do better, so I decided to go back and re-evaluate my approach. I realized that I was trying to do too much at once, so I focused on one area of the project and did it well. After that, the client was happy with my work.

Consultant.question: 185. How did you come to know about our company?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see if the candidate has done his or her homework. It also reveals whether the applicant is familiar with your company and its products or services.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I came across your company while researching the industry. I was impressed by the work you do and thought it would be a great opportunity to learn more about your organization.

Consultant.question: 186. How would you handle a difficult team member?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your ability to work with others and manage conflict. It also gives you insight into the candidate's personality and how they handle stressful situations.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work with others
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand the other person's perspective. I would then try to find a common ground and work toward a solution that is beneficial for both parties. If this doesn't work, I would try to find a compromise that is acceptable for both sides.

Consultant.question: 187. What are your strengths/weaknesses?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test the applicant's self-awareness and ability to communicate effectively. The answer should be well-thought out and specific.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm a strong communicator who is able to build relationships quickly. I'm also a great listener and am able to understand the needs of my clients. I'm always looking for ways to improve my work and am open to feedback. My biggest weakness is that I can get so caught up in the details that I sometimes miss the big picture.

Consultant.question: 188. Why do you want to work in this role at Accenture?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the candidate has done his or her research on the company. Applicants should demonstrate their understanding of Accenture's mission and goals, as well as the role they're applying for.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm very interested in working with Accenture because of its reputation as a global leader in consulting. I've read about the company's vision and goals, and I believe my skills and experience can help Accenture achieve its mission. I'm also interested in working with Accenture because of its focus on innovation. I think it's important to keep up with new technologies and trends, and I want to be a part of that process.

Consultant.question: 189. What are the 3 biggest expenses for a hospital?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the healthcare industry. It also shows how well they can research an industry and understand its challenges.
expectations: Ability to research and understand key issues
Consultant.sampleAnswer: The three biggest expenses for a hospital are labor, supplies and energy. Labor costs are the largest expense for any hospital, and they have been rising steadily for years. Supplies include everything from bandages to pharmaceuticals. Energy costs are also significant because hospitals use a lot of electricity.

Consultant.question: 190. What is a product that you think is overpriced?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the market and ability to think critically. The answer also reveals how the applicant feels about pricing and whether he or she is willing to take a stand.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I think most people would agree that Apple products are overpriced. I've never been a fan of their products, but I know a lot of people who are willing to pay a premium for them. I think Apple is successful because it has a loyal following that is willing to pay more for its products.

Consultant.question: 191. What about a situation where you had a conflict and how did you resolve it?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate handles conflict. It also tests the candidate's ability to work with others and communicate effectively.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I had a situation where I was working with a client who was very difficult to work with. I tried to work with him, but he was very stubborn and wouldn't listen to my advice. I had to find a way to resolve the conflict without losing the client. I spoke with my manager and we decided that it would be best if I worked with someone else on the team. The client was upset at first, but he eventually understood why we made that decision.

Consultant.question: 192. How will you manage your project life cycle?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's understanding of the consulting process. It should be clear that the applicant has experience working with clients and has a plan for managing projects.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I always start by understanding the client's business and goals. I then develop a plan for achieving those goals. I make sure to keep my client in the loop at every step of the way. I believe in communicating openly and honestly with my clients, and I make sure they are always aware of what is happening on their project.

Consultant.question: 193. What skills do you have that would be useful in a consulting role?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's understanding of the skills needed for a consulting role. The answer should show the applicant has thought about what skills they can bring to the table and how those skills will help them succeed in a consulting role.
expectations: Applicant's ability to understand what skills are needed for a consulting role
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have several years of experience working with clients to develop and implement marketing strategies. I've also worked with clients to identify and solve problems that are holding them back from achieving their goals. I believe these skills will be useful in a consulting role because I'm used to working with clients to understand their needs and then developing solutions that meet those needs.

Consultant.question: 194. What experience do you have in the field of logistics and supply chain?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the industry and ability to apply that knowledge to a business. The answer should highlight the applicant's experience in the field and how it can be applied to your company.
expectations: Applicant's knowledge of the logistics and supply chain industry
Ability to apply that knowledge to your company
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've worked with several companies in the logistics and supply chain space. I've helped them improve their operations and increase their efficiency. I've also worked with a few companies that were struggling with supply chain issues. I was able to identify problems and offer solutions that helped them improve their operations.

Consultant.question: 195. How will you differentiate between overloading and overriding a function?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of programming languages. It also shows whether the applicant can think critically and solve problems. The answer should show the candidate's ability to understand the difference between the two concepts and explain how to avoid overloading a function.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Overloading a function means that a function has more than one definition. Overriding a function means that a function has more than one implementation. Overloading is bad because it can lead to ambiguity and confusion. Overriding is good because it allows you to customize a function without changing its definition.

Consultant.question: 196. What is the most difficult situation you have faced and how did you overcome it?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test your ability to handle challenges. It also gives you insight into the applicant's experience and how they deal with problems.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once had a client who was very demanding. He would change his mind often and expect me to adjust my schedule and work late into the night. I had to learn how to set boundaries with him and stick to them. I also had to learn how to say no without upsetting him. In the end, I was able to deliver a great product and keep a good relationship with him.

Consultant.question: 197. What do you know about this job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see if the applicant has done any research on the company or the industry. It also shows how well the applicant can articulate what they know about the job and company.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I know you're a leading provider of IT services in the region. I've read about your work in the industry journal and I'm familiar with your client list. I'm excited to learn more about your business and how I can help you achieve your goals.

Consultant.question: 198. Tell me about a time when you used an innovative solution to solve a complex problem.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to assess your problem-solving skills and ability to think outside the box. Applicants should discuss a time when they were able to use their creativity to find a solution.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think outside the box
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I was working with a company that was experiencing a lot of turnover in its sales department. The company had tried many different tactics to reduce turnover, but nothing seemed to work. I decided to look at the problem from a different angle and discovered that the company's salespeople were not being properly trained. I developed a training program that helped new hires learn the company's products and services more quickly. The program also helped existing employees become more knowledgeable about the products and services they were selling. As a result, turnover decreased significantly.

Consultant.question: 199. What is your expected salary?
Consultant.overview: This question is one of the most common interview questions, but it's also one of the most difficult. The interviewer wants to see how the applicant responds to pressure and how honest they are. The applicant should give a range, not an exact number, and explain why they're seeking that salary.
expectations: Ability to explain why they're seeking a certain salary
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm looking for a salary in the $50,000 to $60,000 range. I feel my experience and skills are worth that amount. I'm also open to negotiation.

Consultant.question: 200. How do you prioritize your tasks?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the candidate manages time and resources. The answer should show that the applicant is organized and can meet deadlines.
expectations: Ability to work well with others
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I prioritize my tasks by importance and urgency. I always make sure I have a clear understanding of what needs to be done and when. I also make sure I have the resources I need to get the job done. I am a very organized person and I like to keep my desk clean and organized. I am also very good at managing my time.

Consultant.question: 201. What experience do you have in leading a team through major changes?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to lead a team through change. The answer should show the applicant's ability to communicate with team members and provide them with the resources they need to succeed.
expectations: Applicant's ability to communicate with team members
Ability to lead a team through change
Ability to manage and motivate a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've led teams through several major changes. One of my most recent projects was helping a company restructure its sales force. The company wanted to increase sales and improve customer service. I worked with the sales team to develop a new strategy and then helped implement it. I started by holding meetings with each salesperson to understand their goals and concerns. I then created a plan that addressed their needs and helped them reach their goals.

Consultant.question: 202. How do you manage stress?
