Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I look for a supervisor who is supportive and fair, and I am comfortable speaking up if I feel that they are not meeting my needs.

Medical Technologist.question: 13. What makes you think that you are eligible for this position?
Medical Technologist.overview: You should ask this question in order to find out why the medical technologist believes they are qualified for the position. The ideal candidate will be able to explain their experience and skills that make them a good fit for the job.
expectations: List of relevant experience and skills
Explanation of how their experience and skills match the job description,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I have five years of experience as a medical technologist, and I have the skills to perform all of the duties required for this position.

Medical Technologist.question: 14. Why did you apply for this job?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is an important question to ask because it shows how the medical technologist views their career. It also shows their motivation for applying for the job and their goals for the future. The ideal candidate will be able to explain why they want to work in your facility and what they hope to accomplish in their career.
expectations: Explanation of why they want to work in your facility
Description of what they hope to accomplish in their career,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I applied for this job because I am looking for a position that will allow me to use my skills and experience in a new setting. I hope to advance my career by working here.

Medical Technologist.question: 15. Could you explain the gaps in your resume?
Medical Technologist.overview: You should ask this question because it shows how the medical technologist explains a gap in their employment. It also shows how they handle negative information about themselves. The ideal candidate will be able to explain the gaps in their employment and will also be able to explain why they left their previous jobs.
expectations: Explanation of reasons for leaving previous jobs,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I took a year off to care for my mother after she was diagnosed with cancer. I left my last job because I was not happy with the work environment.

Medical Technologist.question: 16. How would you compare your previous manager with your current one?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important because it shows how the medical technologist works with a supervisor. It also shows their ability to work with others and their communication skills. The ideal candidate will be able to explain how they work with their current supervisor and what they like and dislike about the relationship.
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I have a good relationship with my supervisor and I feel that she is always willing to help me when I need it.

Medical Technologist.question: 17. What is your greatest strength?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is a great question to ask because it allows you to find out what the medical technologist values in their work. You should also find out how they would describe their work ethic and their ability to work with others. An ideal candidate will be able to explain how they are a team player and how they are able to work well with others.
expectations: Description of their ability to work with others
Description of their ability to work independently,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I am a team player who is able to work well with others. I am also able to work independently when needed.

Medical Technologist.question: 18. Why do you want to work with us?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is an important question to ask because it shows how the medical technologist views your facility. It also shows their level of interest in the position. The ideal candidate will be able to explain why they are interested in working for your company.
expectations: Explanation of why they are interested in the position
Description of how they learned about the position,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I have heard great things about your company and I am excited about the opportunity to work with you.

Medical Technologist.question: 19. Tell me about a time when you had a conflict with your manager?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is an important question to ask because it shows how the medical technologist handles conflict. It also shows how they work with their manager and how they resolve issues. The ideal candidate will be able to explain a time when they had a conflict with their manager and how they resolved it.
expectations: Explanation of how they resolved the conflict
Description of how they work with their manager,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I had a conflict with my manager over the amount of time I was spending on my work, and I was able to resolve the issue by talking with my manager about my workload and getting his input on how to balance my time.

Medical Technologist.question: 20. What makes you a good fit for this position?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important because it allows you to find out what the medical technologist believes makes them a good fit for the position. Their answer should show that they have considered the job requirements and have determined how they meet those requirements.
expectations: List of skills and attributes that make them a good fit
Explanation of how they meet the job requirements,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I have the knowledge and skills to perform the job requirements, and I am also a team player who works well with others.

Medical Technologist.question: 21. How will you respond to receiving a critical value?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is designed to find out how the medical technologist will respond to a critical value. The ideal candidate will be able to explain how they will respond to the situation and what steps they will take to ensure the patient's safety.
expectations: Description of their response to a critical value
Explanation of how they would handle the situation,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I would contact my supervisor and then follow their instructions.

Medical Technologist.question: 22. What is your ultimate goal?
Medical Technologist.overview: You should ask this question in order to find out what the candidate's career goals are. It is important to know if they are looking for a position in the same field or if they are planning to move into a different field. Their answer will also reveal their level of commitment to their career and their willingness to continue to learn.
expectations: Description of how they plan to achieve their goal,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I am looking for a position that will allow me to use my skills and training in order to advance my career.

Medical Technologist.question: 23. What are your values?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important because it shows the candidate's personal values and how they relate to the job. The ideal candidate will be able to explain how their values relate to the job and how they have used their values in their previous positions.
expectations: Description of how values relate to job
Description of how values were used in previous positions,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I value helping others and I use that value in my work by providing excellent patient care.

Medical Technologist.question: 24. What was a business decision you made in the last year, and what were the factors that helped you make your decision?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is an important question to ask a medical technologist because it shows how they make decisions and think on their feet. The ideal candidate will be able to explain their thought process in making the decision, and they will also be able to identify the factors that helped them make the decision.
expectations: Identification of factors that helped them make the decision,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I decided to take a position with a new laboratory because it offered me more opportunities to advance my career.

Medical Technologist.question: 25. What kind of environment do you prefer to work in?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important to ask because it shows the candidate's preference for working in a particular type of environment. It also shows their willingness to work in a variety of settings. An ideal candidate will be able to explain why they prefer the type of environment they have chosen.
expectations: Explanation of why they prefer the environment
Description of how they handle working in other environments,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I prefer to work in a busy emergency room because it keeps me on my toes and allows me to learn new skills quickly.

Medical Technologist.question: 26. What are your strengths and weaknesses?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is a classic interview question that is designed to find out how the candidate will respond to a difficult question. The ideal candidate will be able to identify their weaknesses and explain how they are working to improve them. They should also be able to identify their strengths and explain how they are using them in their current position.
expectations: Explanation of how they are working to improve weaknesses
Description of how they use their strengths,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I am a hard worker who is always willing to learn new skills. My weakness is that I am not always as patient with patients as I should be. I am working on improving my patience by taking a class on meditation.

Medical Technologist.question: 27. What do you expect from your manager?
Medical Technologist.overview: The answer to this question will show how the medical technologist expects to be managed. It will also show how they expect to be treated by their supervisor. An ideal candidate will have a positive attitude and will be willing to work as a team member.
expectations: Willingness to work as a team member
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I expect my manager to give me feedback on my performance and to treat me with respect.

Medical Technologist.question: 28. What is your experience and background?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important because it allows you to find out what the medical technologist's experience is in the medical field. It also allows you to find out if they have any experience in your facility or a similar one.
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I have worked as a medical technologist for five years, and I have experience working in a variety of medical settings.

Medical Technologist.question: 29. What is a difficult situation you have encountered and how did you resolve it?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important because it shows how the medical technologist handles difficult situations. It also shows their problem-solving skills and how they communicate with others. The ideal candidate will be able to explain a situation where they were able to resolve the issue and will also be able to explain how they handled the situation.
expectations: Description of how they resolved the issue
Description of how they handled communication with others,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I was working with a patient who was unable to provide a urine sample for testing. I had to explain the importance of the test and why it was necessary. I was able to get the patient to agree to provide the sample after I explained that it was necessary for his own health.

Medical Technologist.question: 30. Can you tell me about yourself?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is a general question that is asked at the end of an interview. It is a chance for the candidate to summarize their skills and qualifications and to ask for the job.
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I have a Bachelor's degree in Medical Technology and I am certified as a CMT. I have five years of experience in a variety of medical settings and I am able to work independently. I am seeking a position that will allow me to continue to learn and grow in my field.

Medical Technologist.question: 31. How many years of experience do you have?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is an essential question to ask a medical technologist because it shows how long they have been in the field. It also shows their level of experience and their ability to work independently.
expectations: Description of how they got started in the field
Description of any certifications or degrees earned,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I have been a medical technologist for five years. I started working in the field after I graduated from a local community college with an associate degree in medical technology.

Medical Technologist.question: 32. How do you handle stressful situations?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important to ask because it shows how the medical technologist handles stressful situations. It also shows how they handle conflict and how they work under pressure. The ideal candidate will be able to stay calm and will also be able to explain how they handle the situation.
expectations: Explanation of how they handle the situation
Ability to explain the situation to others,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I remain calm and explain the situation to my supervisor.

Medical Technologist.question: 33. What are the responsibilities of a medical technologist?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important because it shows that the candidate is aware of the duties and responsibilities of their job. You may also want to ask them to describe their typical work day or week.
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: My typical work day starts with a meeting with my supervisor to discuss the patients I will be working with that day. I then log into the computer system and document my patients' information. I perform the tests or procedures and then document the results. I then meet with my supervisor again to discuss the results and any concerns.

Medical Technologist.question: 34. When are you available?
Medical Technologist.overview: You should ask this question in order to find out the medical technologist's availability for work. The ideal candidate will be available to work at least one shift per week and will be able to work overtime if needed.
expectations: Availability for at least one shift per week
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I am available to work every other weekend and every other holiday.

Medical Technologist.question: 35. What was your GPA?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is a very important question to ask because it shows the candidate's academic ability. A high GPA shows that they are able to handle a rigorous workload and that they are able to maintain their grades.
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I had a 3.8 GPA in my Bachelor's program and I graduated with honors.

Medical Technologist.question: 36. What is the difference between an esoteric lab and a traditional lab?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important to ask because it shows that the medical technologist is familiar with the different types of labs and their procedures. It also shows their knowledge of the differences between the two types of labs.
expectations: Description of the differences between the two lab types
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: An esoteric lab focuses on tests that are not performed in a traditional lab, such as genetic testing.

Medical Technologist.question: 37. What makes you the best candidate for this job?
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is important because it allows you to find out why the candidate wants the job. It also allows you to find out what they think makes them the best candidate. You should also ask this question to find out what they think are their strengths and weaknesses.
expectations: Explanation of why they want the job
Explanation of what makes them the best candidate
Explanation of their strengths and weaknesses,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I am the best candidate for this job because I have a strong work ethic and I am a fast learner. I also have a strong background in medical technology and I am prepared to learn new skills in my next position.

Medical Technologist.question: 38. Describe a situation where you had to deal with conflict.
Medical Technologist.overview: This question is designed to find out how the candidate handles conflict. You want to know if they are able to resolve the conflict or if they are able to identify the source of the conflict and seek assistance from a supervisor.
expectations: Description of how they handle conflict
Explanation of how they identify the source of conflict,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I try to understand both sides of the conflict and then I try to find a compromise that works for both parties.

Medical Technologist.question: 39. How do you resolve conflicts with your co-workers?
Medical Technologist.overview: This is an important question to ask because it shows how the medical technologist handles stressful situations. It also shows how they work with others. The ideal candidate will be able to resolve conflicts in a calm, professional manner.
expectations: List of steps taken to resolve the conflict
List of steps taken to prevent future conflicts,
Medical Technologist.sampleAnswer: I take a few minutes to collect my thoughts and then I approach the other person and explain the situation in a calm manner. I also try to understand their point of view and then I try to find a solution that works for both of us.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: A: I would notify my shift supervisor and offer to stay until my replacement arrived.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: I would first ensure that the patient had no valid complaints, and then just be patient and reassuring that we were doing everything we could for them.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: The interviewer is asking this open-ended ice-breaker question looking for some introductory information from you. Give a short and engaging response, ending on an interesting note so that the interviewer wants to hear more. At this point, it is more about your personality and ability to give a concise answer than the amount of information you expose. Always tell a story, start by telling them briefly of your past education, and then your past work history, ending with your graduating with your degree and starting your new career. Usually, you would leave out any personal information about yourself, never discuss your age, marital status, children, where you live, hobbies, etc. They are wanting to know about you professionally. Many of those personal questions are illegal to ask in an interview.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Please tell a story – what prompted you to enroll in nursing school and what happened in your life that made you say “I want to be a nurse, I think I will be a great nurse, I can do this”. Tell a succinct story from beginning to end, make it personal.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Whenever you are asked to give an example, please give an example. This question could pertain to anything in life where you had a problem, how you thought it through and came up with a solution. Want they want to know is if you have critical thinking skills.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Again, this could pertain to any area of your life, maybe it was an obstacle with school and family or school and work, etc. Think of a major problem and how you solved it.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Conflict in some manner is usually always asked in some manner during an interview. Always remain positive when discussing former bosses or co-workers. Think about a time you had a conflict with a co-worker and describe how you negotiated and came to a mutually satisfactory resolution.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: A: If the doctor was not happy with my care of a patient in some way, I would want to know how, so I could take corrective action to remedy the situation. If I needed to, I would even bring the question to my supervisor for help resolving the issue.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Honesty is also the best policy when answering this question. It is perfectly acceptable to admit that you feel more comfortable following the lead as you gain more experience. If you are already a seasoned nurse, you can keep it general by saying that your leadership style depends on the situation at hand.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: A: In this situation I would take the following course of action: A) I would bring this concern to the attending doctor and make sure that the patient's pain was being managed in the most effective way. B) I would reassure the patient that everything possible was being done to alleviate their discomfort and C) I would listen sympathetically to their complaint, reassure them that their concerns were being heard, and that we were doing everything possible to help them.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: The interviewer is basically looking for clues that will shed light on your work ethic and interpersonal skills. Direct quotes work well. "Jill always said I was dependable" is a direct quote that says a lot.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Healthcare facilities prefer to hire people who work well with others, have good social skills, get along well with patients and visitors, and can pull together as a team for the sake of patient care.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: In this situation, honesty is the best policy. If you accept a 12-hour night shift position when you are truly a diurnal (daytime) person, your existence might be miserable for months, years, or however long it takes to transfer to day shift. You might also feel bad if you accept a weekend schedule that causes you to miss your children’s Saturday morning sporting events.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Facilities generally shy away from hiring candidates whom they perceive to be job hoppers, so it would be best to indicate that you plan on establishing a long-lasting relationship with the company.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Nursing is not simply a job. It is also a journey filled with lifelong learning. You can discuss the ACLS course you took earlier this year, or the critical care conference you attended recently, or the mental health symposium you visited, or whatever it is you do to maintain or augment your nursing knowledge base.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: I think for me, the most difficult part of being a nurse, is when I have a patient that is very uncomfortable, or in a lot of pain, and I cannot comfort them.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: I would listen to all of their concerns and make sure that if any were well founded, that they were addressed immediately.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: The settings in which nurses work can quickly turn into pressure-cooker environments. To be blunt, the interviewer does not want to hire anyone who is so emotionally fragile that they'll shatter like plate glass when faced with the day-to-day pressures of the job.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: In almost every case, it is important to stress the ability to work with a team over individual contributions, but both are important. While you can certainly function fine on your own, emphasize that you are more of a team player than an individual contributor but can function independently.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: The interviewer wants to hear about strengths that would be assets in the workplace. Since we all have weaknesses, the person conducting the interview will know you're a boldfaced liar if you deny having any.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Your reasons for wanting to work at this place of employment should be positive. Also, make a connection between your career goals and how they can be achieved at this company.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Companies prefer to hire healthcare workers who are motivated by intangible ideals, not concrete realities such as money. Even if cash is your ultimate motivation, do not elaborate on your need for money.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: Ask the interviewer a question or two, whether it pertains to nurse/patient ratios, length of orientation, or educational opportunities. You might appear uninterested if you have no questions

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: If you have healthcare experience, they want to know how you have dealt with angry doctors, emotionally upset families, or difficult patients. If you lack healthcare experience, you can discuss a difficult situation that occurred in school or a previous workplace.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: We’ve all made mistakes, so be honest. The mistake that you divulge may or may not be related to nursing. For example: “I used to delay charting until the very end of each shift, but realized I wasn’t making the most of my time. I’ve learned to chart during the shift to improve my time management.”

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: You can discuss an achievement that is either linked to nursing or totally unrelated to nursing. Many nurses say that attaining their nursing degree has been their greatest achievement. Others state that forming a family has been their greatest achievement because it has given them a greater understanding of the human experience.

Nursing.question: Q: What would you do if your shift replacement did not arrive on time or at all?
Nursing.sampleAnswer: This is the last time to truly sell yourself to the interviewer. Emphasize your positive attributes, reaffirm that you are a team player, and tell them why you are the best candidate for the position that they need to fill.

Occupational Therapist.question: 1. Where do you see yourself in 5 years time?
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists are in high demand in the workforce. They are needed in hospitals, clinics, rehabilitation centers and private practices. They work with patients with a variety of injuries and disabilities. The therapist is dedicated to helping patients recover and get back to work.
expectations: Commitment to helping patients get back to work
Career goals that include helping patients and the community,
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: I see myself working as an occupational therapist in a private practice. I will continue to help injured workers recover from their injuries and get back to work. I will also continue to help patients with disabilities achieve their goals and live more independent lives.

Occupational Therapist.question: 2. What was the most difficult situation you've been in at work?
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists work with patients who have a wide range of injuries and disabilities. They must remain patient and understanding as they help patients recover from their injuries. They need to remain calm and focused when the patient is frustrated or angry.
expectations: Experience working with patients who are frustrated
Ability to remain focused under pressure,
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: I worked with a patient who was frustrated after his injury and had difficulty accepting his new limitations. He was angry and upset with his situation and lashed out at me. I remained calm and focused on helping him understand the importance of his recovery and how it would help him get back to work.

Occupational Therapist.question: 3. What is your experience as a therapist?
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists work with patients who have physical and mental disabilities. They conduct assessments to gauge the individual's abilities and create plans to help the workers complete daily tasks required for their preferred jobs. The plans include rehabilitative services related to the individual's injuries and the best practices for getting them back into the workforce.
expectations: Experience working as an occupational therapist
Examples of skill cultivation in previous patients
Overall subject knowledge and communication skills,
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: I worked as an occupational therapist for several years. I conducted assessments on patients and created customized rehabilitation plans to help them regain lost skills. I helped patients who had suffered from injuries or disabilities return to work.

Occupational Therapist.question: 4. Tell me about a difficult client you had and how did you address the issue.
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists work with patients who have a variety of injuries and disabilities. They must be patient and understanding as they treat patients who don't progress at the same rate. They are also required to manage care for injured workers on a daily basis.
expectations: Experience working with patients with varying injuries
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: I worked with a patient who had a permanent disability that prevented him from progressing at the same rate as other patients. I was patient and understanding as I worked with him to achieve new goals. I also managed his care on a daily basis and coordinated with his physician to ensure he received the best treatment possible.

Occupational Therapist.question: 5. What are your strengths and weaknesses?
Occupational Therapist.overview: The interviewer wants to know what you consider your strengths and weaknesses. You should be prepared to discuss both.
expectations: Examples of your strengths and weaknesses
Explanation of how you have used your strengths to overcome your weaknesses,
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: My greatest strength is my ability to remain patient with my patients. I have worked with many people who have been through a lot, and I understand that it takes time to recover from injuries. My greatest weakness is my lack of knowledge in the medical field. I have always been interested in medicine, but I have not had the opportunity to study it.

Occupational Therapist.question: 6. Tell me about a time when you had to deal with a difficult patient.
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists work with patients who have a variety of injuries and disabilities. Some patients are more challenging than others, and the therapist must remain patient and calm when working with them. They must also be able to identify the patient's needs and provide the best care to meet those needs.
expectations: Experience working with patients who have a variety of injuries and disabilities
Dedication and care toward patient success,
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: I worked with a patient who was very frustrated with his progress after his injury. He was unable to complete the tasks that he needed to do to return to work. I remained calm and patient as I worked with him to set new goals that were more realistic for his current abilities.

Occupational Therapist.question: 7. Can you tell me more about your experience?
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists work with patients who have suffered injuries and disabilities. They help patients regain their abilities and return to the workforce. They conduct assessments to gauge the individual's progress and create plans to help the workers complete daily tasks required for their preferred jobs. The plans include rehabilitative services related to the individual's injuries and the best practices for getting them back into the workforce.
expectations: Examples of skill cultivation in previous clients
Overall subject knowledge and communication skills,
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: My rehabilitation plans started with a complete assessment of the individual's skills set. I built plans to strengthen weaknesses and enhance the individual's strengths. I compared their benchmark results with the current requirements for their preferred job.

Occupational Therapist.question: 8. Tell me about a time when you had conflict with your supervisor.
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists work with patients who have varying injuries and disabilities. They must be able to work with patients who don't progress at the same rate. They must also be patient and well-organized when treating patients. The therapist understands what it takes to manage care for injured workers on a daily basis.
expectations: Experience working with patients with varying injuries
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: I had a conflict with my supervisor when I disagreed with her about the patient's treatment plan. I felt that the patient wasn't progressing at the same rate as others and wanted to change the treatment plan. I presented my case to her and she agreed that we should change the plan.

Occupational Therapist.question: 9. What do you do to provide exceptional patient care?
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists are patient and understanding when working with patients. They provide the best care possible and help patients achieve their goals. They are compassionate and dedicated to helping patients recover from injuries and return to work.
expectations: Dedication to helping patients achieve their goals
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: I provided exceptional care by being patient with my patients and helping them achieve their goals. I was compassionate and understanding when working with them, and I helped them recover from their injuries and return to work.

Occupational Therapist.question: 10. What is it about this setting that interests you?
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists work with injured workers to help them regain their skills and return to their jobs. They work in a variety of settings, including hospitals, rehabilitation centers, private practices and more. The therapist must be able to work with patients who have varying injuries and disabilities.
expectations: Experience working with patients with varying injuries and disabilities
Interest in working in a variety of settings
Interest in working with patients who have physical and mental disabilities,
Occupational Therapist.sampleAnswer: I've always been interested in helping people recover from injuries and get back to their jobs. I'm interested in working in a variety of settings, including hospitals, rehabilitation centers, private practices and more.

Occupational Therapist.question: 11. Why are you interested in this position?
Occupational Therapist.overview: Occupational therapists work with patients who have a variety of injuries and disabilities. They help the patients recover and return to their preferred jobs. The therapist must be patient and caring, and they must be able to work with a variety of patients.
expectations: Experience working with patients with varying injuries
Dedication to helping patients achieve their goals

Pediatric SLPs.question: 1. How do you keep up with due dates and important to-do items?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question assesses your organizational skills and time management strategies, both critical in the fast-paced environment of pediatric speech therapy. The interviewer wants to know how you ensure that all tasks are completed on time, especially in a setting that often requires juggling multiple responsibilities.
expectations: Clear time management strategies Use of tools or systems for organization Ability to prioritize tasks effectively Demonstration of reliability and consistency
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: To manage due dates and important tasks, I rely on a combination of digital tools and a traditional planner. I use calendar apps and task management tools like Trello or Google Keep to set reminders for key deadlines and track ongoing tasks. Additionally, I maintain a daily checklist in my planner to prioritize tasks and ensure that nothing falls through the cracks. This system allows me to stay organized and meet deadlines consistently, ensuring that I’m always prepared for IEP meetings, report submissions, and therapy sessions.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 2. How do you organize therapy data and session notes?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question tests your ability to handle documentation, which is essential for tracking progress and communicating with parents and other professionals. The interviewer is looking for a systematic approach to data management that ensures accuracy and accessibility.
expectations: Clear explanation of your documentation process Use of tools or methods to organize data Emphasis on accuracy and ease of access Consideration of confidentiality and security
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: I organize therapy data and session notes using a combination of digital and paper-based systems, depending on the setting. For digital records, I use secure software that allows me to input session notes immediately after therapy and track progress over time. I categorize data by goals and objectives, making it easy to review and share with parents or other team members. For paper-based systems, I keep detailed logs in individual student folders, organized by session date and type of intervention. This ensures that I have quick access to accurate records, which is crucial for tracking progress and adjusting therapy plans as needed.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 3. What’s your philosophy for serving preschool students for speech/language?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question explores your approach to early intervention and how you view your role in supporting preschool-aged children. The interviewer wants to understand your core beliefs and strategies for fostering speech and language development in young learners.
expectations: Articulation of a clear and thoughtful philosophy Emphasis on the importance of early intervention Focus on child-centered, play-based, and family-inclusive approaches Understanding of developmentally appropriate practices
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: My philosophy for serving preschool students centers on the belief that early intervention is key to successful communication development. I focus on creating a playful and engaging environment where children feel comfortable exploring language. I use play-based activities that are developmentally appropriate and tailored to each child’s interests and needs. I also believe in involving families in the process, as their support is crucial for reinforcing skills outside of therapy. By building a strong foundation in the preschool years, I aim to empower children with the communication tools they need for lifelong success.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 4. What model do you currently use to serve students? (pull out, push in, inclusion, collaborative, coteaching, coaching, consultation?)
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question assesses your experience with different service delivery models and your flexibility in adapting to various educational settings. The interviewer is looking for your rationale behind using a specific model and how it aligns with the needs of the students you serve.
expectations: Explanation of the model(s) you use Justification for why the chosen model is effective Willingness to adapt based on student needs and school environment Examples of how the model benefits students
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: Currently, I primarily use a push-in model for serving students, as I believe that integrating speech and language services within the classroom setting allows for more naturalistic learning opportunities. By collaborating with teachers, I can address speech and language goals within the context of the curriculum, which helps students generalize skills more effectively. However, I also use a pull-out model when more intensive, individualized instruction is needed. I’m flexible and willing to adapt my approach based on the needs of the students and the preferences of the school, ensuring that each child receives the support that best suits their learning style.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 5. Tell me a little bit about yourself.
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This is often an icebreaker question that gives you a chance to present a summary of your professional background, key skills, and what drives you as an SLP. The interviewer is looking for a concise yet compelling narrative that highlights your qualifications and passion for the field
expectations: Brief professional background Key skills and areas of expertise Personal motivation or passion for the field Connection to the role you’re applying for
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: I’m a licensed Speech-Language Pathologist with over five years of experience working primarily with pediatric populations. My journey into speech-language pathology began with a deep interest in communication disorders and a passion for helping children find their voice. Over the years, I’ve specialized in early intervention and autism spectrum disorders, with a focus on using play-based and family-centered approaches. I’m excited about this opportunity because it aligns with my goal of providing high-quality, individualized care to children in a supportive and collaborative environment.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 6. What social skills resources do you use for children with autism spectrum disorders?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question assesses your knowledge of resources and interventions for children with autism. The interviewer is looking for specific tools and strategies you employ to enhance social skills development in this population.
expectations: Specific resources or programs used Explanation of how these resources are applied in therapy Understanding of how resources meet the unique needs of children with autism Examples of positive outcomes from using these resources
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: For children with autism, I often use a combination of visual supports, social stories, and evidence-based programs like the Social Thinking curriculum. Visual supports help to clarify expectations and reduce anxiety, while social stories provide concrete examples of appropriate social behavior in various contexts. Additionally, I incorporate peer modeling and role-playing activities to practice these skills in a supportive environment. These resources have been instrumental in helping my students improve their social interactions and build confidence in navigating social situations.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 7. What prompted you to want a career in speech-language pathology?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question delves into your personal motivation for choosing this career path. The interviewer is interested in your passion for the field and the experiences that inspired you to become an SLP.
expectations: Personal story or motivation Reflection on key experiences that influenced your decision Connection between your passion and the role Enthusiasm for the field
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: My interest in speech-language pathology began in college when I volunteered at a clinic that served children with communication disorders. Seeing the transformative impact that therapy had on these children and their families inspired me to pursue this career. I was particularly drawn to the combination of science and human connection that this field offers. Every day, I’m motivated by the opportunity to help children find their voice and reach their full potential, which is why I’m excited about this role and the chance to continue making a difference.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 8. Who are your mentors, and how have they guided you in your career path?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question explores the influences on your professional development. The interviewer wants to understand who has shaped your career and how their guidance has impacted your practice.
expectations: Identification of key mentors Specific examples of how they’ve guided your career Reflection on the lessons learned from them Demonstration of ongoing professional growth
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: One of my key mentors was my clinical supervisor during my CFY year. She taught me the importance of combining evidence-based practice with a compassionate, individualized approach to therapy. Her guidance helped me develop strong clinical skills, particularly in managing complex cases. Another mentor is a seasoned SLP who specializes in autism interventions. She introduced me to various social skills programs and has been instrumental in refining my approaches to working with this population. Their insights have shaped my career and continue to inspire me to seek out new learning opportunities and challenges.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 9. What’s most important to you in your job hunt?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question assesses your priorities and what you value in a work environment. The interviewer is looking for insight into what motivates you and how well your goals align with the organization’s offerings.
expectations: Clear identification of key priorities (e.g., work-life balance, professional development, patient population) Connection between your priorities and the role/organization Reflection on how these priorities contribute to your job satisfaction
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: What’s most important to me in my job hunt is finding a position where I can continue to grow professionally while making a meaningful impact on the lives of the children I work with. I’m looking for a supportive environment that values collaboration and provides opportunities for continuing education. Additionally, I’m drawn to settings where I can work with diverse pediatric populations, as I enjoy the challenge of tailoring interventions to meet each child’s unique needs. This role seems like a perfect fit because it offers both professional development and the chance to work in a dynamic, child-focused environment.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 10. What are your favorite settings/special populations to work with?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question seeks to understand your preferences and expertise in various work settings or with specific populations. The interviewer wants to know where your passion lies and how your experience aligns with the needs of the position.
expectations: Identification of preferred settings or populations Explanation of why you enjoy working in those settings or with those populations Connection to the role you’re applying for Examples of successful outcomes in those settings/populations
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: I particularly enjoy working in early intervention settings and with preschool-aged children. There’s something incredibly rewarding about helping young children develop foundational communication skills that set them up for success in school and life. I also have a strong interest in working with children on the autism spectrum, as I find the work challenging yet deeply fulfilling. Tailoring interventions to meet their unique communication needs and seeing the progress they make is what drives me. This role appeals to me because it focuses on early childhood, and I’m excited about the opportunity to apply my skills and passion here.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 11. What continuing education courses have you taken in the past 2 years?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question evaluates your commitment to ongoing professional development. The interviewer wants to see how you stay current in the field and how recent learning has influenced your practice.
expectations: List of relevant continuing education courses Explanation of how these courses have enhanced your skills Connection between your learning and its practical application in therapy Demonstration of a proactive approach to professional growth
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: In the past two years, I’ve taken several continuing education courses, including a certification in PROMPT therapy, a course on early intervention strategies for children with autism, and a workshop on using AAC devices in pediatric populations. These courses have significantly expanded my toolkit, allowing me to provide more tailored and effective interventions. For instance, my PROMPT training has improved my ability to address motor speech disorders, and the AAC workshop has given me new strategies for supporting nonverbal children. I’m committed to lifelong learning and continuously seeking opportunities to enhance my practice.

Pediatric SLPs.question: 12. Are you certified in any therapy program such as Hanen, Floortime, ABA, Lindamood Bell, etc.?
Pediatric SLPs.overview: This question assesses your qualifications and expertise in specialized therapy programs. The interviewer wants to know if you bring any additional certifications that can enhance your practice and benefit the population you serve.
expectations: Identification of any relevant certifications Explanation of how these certifications have impacted your practice Reflection on how these programs align with the needs of the population you work with Demonstration of ongoing commitment to professional development
Pediatric SLPs.sampleAnswer: Yes, I’m certified in the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" program, which has been incredibly valuable in my work with young children and their families. This certification has deepened my understanding of parent-child interaction and provided me with practical strategies to empower parents as active participants in their child’s language development. I’ve also completed training in Floortime, which I use to support children with autism by meeting them where they are developmentally and building on their strengths. These certifications have enhanced my ability to provide comprehensive, family-centered care.
