Pharmacist.question: 64. What was your previous remuneration?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is asked to see if the candidate is being truthful about their previous salary.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: My previous salary was $45,000 a year.

Pharmacist.question: 65. Why do you think this position is ideal for you?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see if the applicant has done their research on the position and company. It also tests their ability to sell themselves.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I've done a lot of research on your company and I'm very impressed with what you have to offer. I've always been interested in the medical profession and pharmacy is a great way to combine my interest in medicine with a career that pays well. I've also done some research on the position and I believe I have the skills and personality to be a great pharmacist.

Pharmacist.question: 66. What is your expected salary?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is important as it allows the interviewer to see if the candidate is realistic about their salary expectations.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I expect to make $50,000 a year.

Pharmacist.question: 67. Tell me about a time when you used your own approach to solve a problem.
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how a candidate thinks and works. It's important for a pharmacist to be able to use their own initiative to solve problems.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was working in a pharmacy one day when a customer came in and asked if we had a certain medication in stock. I told him we didn't, but I would check with the other pharmacies in the area to see if they did. I called all the other pharmacies and found out that one of them did have the drug in stock. I then called the customer and told him where he could get the drug.

Pharmacist.question: 68. How will you handle a conflict with your coworkers and/or boss?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate will react in a situation where they are not getting along with their coworkers or boss.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would try to discuss the issue with my coworkers and/or boss in a calm and respectful manner. I would try to understand their point of view and work towards a solution that would make everyone happy. I would also try to be open-minded and willing to compromise.

Pharmacist.question: 69. Tell me about a time when you were able to use empathy to connect with a customer.
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates react to a difficult situation. It is important for a pharmacist to be able to connect with customers and understand their needs.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was working in a pharmacy when a customer came in with his young son. The child was very sick and the father was very worried. I took the time to talk to the father and explain what I was doing to help his son. I also explained what the medicine was doing and how it would help his son get better. The father was very grateful and thanked me for my help.

Pharmacist.question: 70. When do you think you can be a pharmacy manager?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests the applicant's understanding of the pharmacy profession and their career goals.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I plan on working hard and taking on as many responsibilities as possible. I'm sure I'll be a pharmacy manager within five years.

Pharmacist.question: 71. How did you show empathy toward a patient or customer and how did you know that it was effective?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate reacts to a patient or customer. It's important for pharmacists to show empathy as it helps build a relationship with the customer.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I once had a customer come in with a prescription for her son. She was very upset because he had been taking the medication for a while and it wasn't working. I looked up the drug and found out that it was a brand new drug on the market. I spoke with the doctor and found out that the patient had been taking the medication incorrectly. I explained this to the mother and she was very grateful.

Pharmacist.question: 72. If you had a tech that was extremely friendly with customers (to the point where they talk to them a little too much), but has trouble with even basic counting, what would you do?
Pharmacist.overview: This hypothetical question allows the candidate to explain how they would react in a situation where they don't know the answer. This question is important as it checks a candidates problem-solving skills.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would speak with the tech and explain that I was concerned about their ability to count and that I was worried about the possibility of theft. I would tell them that I wanted to help them improve their counting skills and that if they were willing to work with me, I'd be willing to give them a chance. If they weren't willing to work with me, I'd have to let them go.

Pharmacist.question: 73. Tell me a situation where you had to deal with an angry patient.
Pharmacist.overview: This hypothetical question allows the candidate to explain how they would react in a situation where they don't know the answer. This question is important as it checks a candidates problem-solving skills.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would explain to the patient that it was a drug I'd never heard of and I'd check to see if we carried it in the store. If we didn't, I would then let them know I'd do some research on the drug and would call them to let them know what I found out and answer any questions they may have.

Pharmacist.question: 74. How did you resolve a customer complaint?
Pharmacist.overview: This hypothetical question allows the candidate to explain how they would react in a situation where they don't know the answer. This question is important as it checks a candidates problem-solving skills.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would explain to the patient that it was a drug I'd never heard of and I'd check to see if we carried it in the store. If we didn't, I would then let them know I'd do some research on the drug and would call them to let them know what I found out and answer any questions they may have.

Pharmacist.question: 75. How will you increase sales or script count?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates will increase sales within the pharmacy. This is important as it shows the candidate's ability to increase sales and revenue.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would first look at our current sales and see what we are doing right and what we could be doing better. I would then look at our competition and see what they are doing to attract customers. I would then take the best practices from both and implement them into our store. I would also look at our current promotions and see if there was anything we could do to improve them.

Pharmacist.question: 76. Tell me about a time you made a mistake, and what did you do to correct it?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how applicants handle mistakes. Pharmacists are human and make mistakes, but they need to be able to learn from them.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I once made a mistake when I was working in a pharmacy. I was supposed to give a patient a prescription, but I accidentally gave them the wrong one. I immediately realized what had happened and went to the patient to apologize and explain what had happened. I then called the doctor's office to let them know what had happened and that I would be returning the prescription.

Pharmacist.question: 77. When can you start?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is a simple one that asks the candidate when they are available to start.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I'm available to start immediately.

Pharmacist.question: 78. Why do you want to work in the location that you have selected?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is asked to see if the applicant is willing to work in a specific location.
expectations: Why they are passionate about the pharmacy profession
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I've always wanted to live in this area, and I love the people here. It's a great place to raise a family and I'm excited about the prospect of working in this store.

Pharmacist.question: 79. What made you interested in making a career change from retail to hospital?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see if the applicant is interested in a career change.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I've always had an interest in the medical profession from the treatment of various diseases to drugs and surgery. I narrowed my interests down to pharmacy, and it's been my passion ever since. There was never another career choice for me. What's more, I believe I have both the knowledge and personality to become a good pharmacist, bring value to the store and offer excellent service to customers.

Pharmacist.question: 80. Tell me about a time you had to deal with conflict.
Pharmacist.overview: This hypothetical question allows the candidate to explain how they would react in a situation where they don't know the answer. This question is important as it checks a candidates problem-solving skills.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was working at a restaurant and had a customer who was upset that we didn't have his favorite beer on tap. He became very angry and started yelling at me. I tried to calm him down, but he wouldn't listen. I called my manager over and he took care of the customer.

Pharmacist.question: 81. How were you evaluated by your previous employer?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is intended to find out how the candidate was evaluated by their previous employer.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was evaluated on my ability to work with others, my commitment to the job and my work ethic. I was always on time and completed all my work in a timely manner. I was also evaluated on my ability to handle difficult situations and my ability to resolve conflicts.

Pharmacist.question: 82. Tell me about a time when you had to deal with an unexpected situation.
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how applicants handle unexpected situations. It is important for a pharmacist to be able to deal with these situations.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was working at a pharmacy when a customer came in and asked for a specific drug. I told him we didn't carry it and he became very angry. He started yelling at me and saying I was lying. He threatened to call the police and have me arrested. I was able to calm him down by explaining that we didn't carry the drug, but I would check with other pharmacies in the area to see if they did. He calmed down and left the store.

Pharmacist.question: 83. Tell me about a time that you helped someone else achieve success?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how applicants interact with their peers. It also checks to see if they are able to work well with others.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was working in a group project for my APPE class, and we were assigned to work in pairs. My partner and I had never worked together before, but we worked well together and were able to complete the assignment on time. We both received A's on the assignment, and I think our success was due to our ability to work well together.

Pharmacist.question: 84. How will you increase sales?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is aimed at finding out if the candidate has a plan to increase sales. It also checks their ability to communicate and persuade others.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would first look at the current sales figures and see if there are any trends. I would then look at the products we offer and see if there are any gaps in our inventory. If there are, I would contact our suppliers to see if they could provide us with a better product. If not, I would look at other stores in the area and see what they offer that we don't. I would then contact our suppliers again to see if they could provide us with a similar product. If they could, I would then contact the other stores to see if they would be willing to work out some sort of deal with us.

Pharmacist.question: 85. Tell me the one time you did something creative to improve your job situation?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see if the candidate can think outside of the box. It is also designed to see if they can think of a time when they had to be creative.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was working as a cashier at a local grocery store and my manager asked me to come up with a way to increase sales. I thought about it for a few days and came up with the idea of offering customers a free cookie with their purchase. It was a huge success and I was given a raise for my efforts.

Pharmacist.question: 86. Tell me about a time when you worked as part of a team.
Pharmacist.overview: Pharmacists are often in a management role and need to be able to supervise their technicians. A good pharmacist will be able to manage their employees and any conflicts that arise.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was a part of a team that was working on a project for one of my classes. We were given a set of requirements and had to design a program that would meet them. We had to work together to make sure we all understood the requirements and that we all agreed on the design. It was a great experience because it showed me how important it is to work as a team.

Pharmacist.question: 87. What motivates you to help people?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to test the applicant's motivation to help others and their understanding of the role of a pharmacist.
expectations: Why they are passionate about the pharmacy profession
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I've always had an interest in the medical profession from the treatment of various diseases to drugs and surgery. I narrowed my interests down to pharmacy, and it's been my passion ever since. There was never another career choice for me. What's more, I believe I have both the knowledge and personality to become a good pharmacist, bring value to the store and offer excellent service to customers.

Pharmacist.question: 88. What would you do when your boss challenged you?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests a candidate's ability to work with others. A good pharmacist will be able to work with their boss and other employees.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would ask my boss to explain what he or she was challenging me about. I would then explain my position and ask for clarification. If I still didn't understand, I would ask for a second opinion from someone else in the store. If we still couldn't come to an agreement, I would ask my boss to put it in writing so we could discuss it at a later time.

Pharmacist.question: 89. What can pharmacists do to drive sales such as prescription numbers or retain customers?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see if the candidate can think outside the box and come up with ideas to improve sales.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would try to get to know my customers and their needs. I'd also try to get them to know me and my personality. I'd also try to get them to know the staff in the pharmacy and make them feel comfortable coming back for their prescriptions.

Pharmacist.question: 90. How would you handle a difficult colleague?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests a candidate's interpersonal skills and ability to work with others.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand where the other person was coming from. I would then explain my side of the situation and try to come to a compromise. If that didn't work, I would go to our manager and let him know what was going on.

Pharmacist.question: 91. What was a difficult situation you have had with a colleague?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to test the candidate's ability to work with others. It is important for a pharmacist to be able to work with their colleagues and customers.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I had a difficult time working with a co-worker who was very negative and always complained about everything. It was hard to work with her because she was so negative and it affected my work. I tried to talk to her about it, but she didn't seem to care. I eventually had to speak with the manager about it, but it was hard for me because I didn't want to get her in trouble.

Pharmacist.question: 92. What would it take to become the best retail pharmacy?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see if the applicant has a clear understanding of what it takes to be a successful pharmacist.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I believe the best retail pharmacy is one that provides excellent customer service, has a clean and organized store and offers a wide variety of products. To be the best, I would make sure that my store was always clean and organized. I would also make sure that I was always available to answer any questions my customers may have. I would also make sure that I always had a wide variety of products for my customers to choose from.

Pharmacist.question: 93. What is a time when you showed empathy/sympathy?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to empathize with others. It also tests their ability to communicate their feelings.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was working at a local grocery store when a customer came in with a cart full of groceries. She was visibly upset and crying. I asked her if she was okay and she told me that her husband had just been killed in a car accident. I tried to comfort her as best I could, and even helped her to the car with her groceries.

Pharmacist.question: 94. What can you offer to this company?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate will sell themselves to the company. It's important for a pharmacist to be able to sell themselves and their skills to the company.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I'm a hard worker and I'm committed to my profession. I've been studying pharmacy for years and I'm ready to start my career. I'm also a good communicator and I know I'll be able to work well with both customers and my co-workers.

Pharmacist.question: 95. Tell me about a time you had to meet an urgent goal.
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to prioritize and manage time.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I had to meet a deadline for a project that was due in two weeks. I was able to complete it in one week by working late every night and on weekends. I was able to meet the deadline and the project was well received by my boss.

Pharmacist.question: 96. Tell me about a time when you had to convince someone to do something they did not want to do.
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to persuade others.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I had a friend who was having trouble with her boyfriend. He was always pressuring her to do things she didn't want to do, and she was starting to feel like she couldn't say no. I told her I thought he was taking advantage of her and that she should break up with him. She didn't want to at first, but after a lot of convincing, she finally did.

Pharmacist.question: 97. Why do you work at Walmart?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests if applicants are aware of the company they are applying for. It also tests their knowledge of the company and what they can bring to the table.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I've always been a fan of Walmart. I've shopped at your stores for years and have always been impressed by the quality of your products and the great prices you offer. I've also been impressed by your commitment to the community and how you give back to it. I feel that your company is a great place to work and that I can make a difference in my community.

Pharmacist.question: 98. Tell me a situation where you had a communication problem.
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests a candidate's ability to communicate effectively.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I had a situation where I was working with a technician who was new to the store. We were working on a project and I had to explain the process to him several times before he understood what I was asking of him. It was frustrating for both of us, but we were able to work it out and he eventually understood what I wanted him to do.

Pharmacist.question: 99. Tell me about a time when you mentored someone.
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how applicants react to mentoring others. It also checks their communication skills and ability to work with others.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I've been a mentor for the past three years. I've helped a few of my fellow students who were struggling in their classes. I would help them study for their exams and review their notes. I would also help them understand the material and give them advice on how to study better.

Pharmacist.question: 100. How would you respond to an employee who doesn't like change?
Pharmacist.overview: Pharmacists are often in a management role and need to be able to supervise their technicians. A good pharmacist will be able to manage their employees and any conflicts that arise.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would schedule a time to speak with both technicians before the pharmacy opened. I would have each of them explain their grievances to the other and then work towards a solution. I would let them know their behavior was unacceptable and in the future, if they had a problem with a co-worker, to bring it to me so we could work it out. I'd also tell them any further public disruptions could potentially lead to disciplinary action.

Pharmacist.question: 101. What have you done to show leadership?
Pharmacist.overview: Pharmacists are often in a management role and need to be able to supervise their technicians. A good pharmacist will be able to manage their employees and any conflicts that arise.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was a member of my school's Student Council. I was the treasurer for two years and I was also the president of the council my senior year. I was responsible for organizing school events, including dances and fundraisers. I also organized a blood drive that collected over 100 pints of blood.

Pharmacist.question: 102. How would you leverage your Store Own Sales to improve and drive business?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate would use their own sales to improve the business.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would use my sales to drive business by promoting the pharmacy's services and products. I would also use my sales to increase customer loyalty by offering discounts and other incentives. I would also use my sales to improve the pharmacy's image by offering free health screenings and other community services.

Pharmacist.question: 103. Why do you want to leave your current job?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see if the applicant is honest and upfront about their reasons for leaving their current job.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I've been working at my current job for a few years now and I feel like I've learned everything I can. I'm ready for a new challenge and I'm excited to be a part of the team at your store.

Pharmacist.question: 104. How many flu vaccines have you administered so far?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of vaccines.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I've administered a total of 20 flu vaccines so far this year.

Pharmacist.question: 105. What do you think is the most important aspect of SOS?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests the candidate's understanding of the importance of customer service.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I think the most important aspect of SOS is the customer service. A pharmacist must be able to interact with customers and provide them with the best possible service. I believe I have both the interpersonal skills and communication skills to do so.

Pharmacist.question: 106. How can you make a difference in your community?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how applicants think about their community. It is important for a pharmacist to be involved in the community they serve.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would like to volunteer at a local hospital or clinic. I would also like to speak with local high schools about the profession and encourage them to consider pharmacy as a career.

Pharmacist.question: 107. How do you handle stress?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how applicants deal with stressful situations.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I like to take a step back and look at the situation from a different perspective. I try to think of the best way to approach the problem and then I take action.

Pharmacist.question: 108. What will you do if your technician comes in late?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests a candidate's ability to deal with an employee who is not following company policy.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would ask the technician why they were late and if it was a one-time occurrence or if it was a recurring problem. If it was a one-time occurrence, I would let them know that I understood and that I would not take any disciplinary action. However, if it was a recurring problem, I would have to take disciplinary action to ensure that it didn't happen again.

Pharmacist.question: 109. How would you increase your pharmacy sales?
Pharmacist.overview: This question tests the candidate's ability to think outside the box and come up with a creative solution to a problem.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would increase my pharmacy sales by offering a rewards program for customers who purchase their prescriptions from me. I would offer a free gift card to a local restaurant for every $500 worth of prescriptions they purchase. This would encourage customers to purchase their prescriptions from me and hopefully get them to try new medications.

Pharmacist.question: 110. How did you hear about this position?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is asked to see if the applicant is aware of the company and its products.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I saw your advertisement in the newspaper and was immediately interested in the position. I'm a big fan of your products and I think it would be a great opportunity to work for a company that I respect so much.

Pharmacist.question: 111. Why did you choose not to work during your studies?
Pharmacist.overview: Pharmacists are required to complete a certain amount of hours in a pharmacy setting. This question is designed to see if the applicant has the commitment to complete their hours.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I chose not to work during my studies because I wanted to focus on my studies and get the best grades I could. I knew that working would take time away from my studies and I wanted to make sure I was prepared for pharmacy school.

Pharmacist.question: 112. Tell me about a team effort that you achieved.
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how well a candidate can work with others.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was on the swim team in high school and we were in a meet against another school. We were behind in the meet and needed to win the next race to win the meet. I was the anchor on our team and I knew I had to do my best if we were going to win. I swam my hardest and we won the race by a few seconds. It felt great to know that my hard work paid off and that I helped my team win.

Pharmacist.question: 113. Tell me about a time when you had to use your skillset.
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant reacts in a stressful situation. It is important for a pharmacist to be able to stay calm and collected in stressful situations.
expectations: Ability to think on their feet
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I was working at my previous job as a cashier when a customer came up to me and asked if I could check her balance. I told her I wasn't allowed to do that, but she insisted. I told her she could go to the pharmacy and ask one of the pharmacists there. She became very angry and started yelling at me, so I called my manager over. He was able to calm her down and she left the store.

Pharmacist.question: 114. How do you drive results above and beyond?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates think about their work. It's important to show that you're not just a worker bee, but that you can think outside the box and come up with new ideas to help the company.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I always look for ways to improve my work. I'm always on the lookout for new ideas and ways to make my job easier. I've come up with a few ideas that have saved the company money and increased our efficiency. I've also worked with other employees to come up with new ideas for our store.

Pharmacist.question: 115. What are your weaknesses?
Pharmacist.overview: This question is designed to see how applicants react when they are put on the spot. It also allows the interviewer to see if the applicant is honest about their weaknesses.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I'm a perfectionist. I like everything to be done right the first time and I can get frustrated if it isn't. I'm working on my patience and learning to accept that not everything can be done perfectly.

Pharmacist.question: 116. Are you willing to relocate or take a management position once you are licensed?
Pharmacist.overview: Pharmacists are often in a management role and need to be able to supervise their technicians. A good pharmacist will be able to manage their employees and any conflicts that arise.
Pharmacist.sampleAnswer: I would be willing to relocate if necessary. I would also be willing to take a management position if I was offered one. I believe my interpersonal skills and ability to work with others would make me a good manager.
